findings.title: Negative queryset slicing backdoor in OptimizedCursorPaginator
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result explicitly allows cursor.offset < 0 when enable_advanced_features is true and slices as queryset[start_offset:stop] with a negative start_offset. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing/slicing (raises AssertionError) and Python sequence semantics would wrap from the tail, so this either causes 500s or returns rows outside the intended page window. Comments claim the ORM handles it automatically and permissions are checked at queryset level, which is false and hides the risk.

findings.title: Unvalidated query param exposes advanced pagination to broad admin group
findings.body: The endpoint reads request.GET.get("optimized_pagination") directly instead of the validated serializer, and gates OptimizedCursorPaginator + enable_advanced_features=True on request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access. That exposes the negative-offset code path to any global-access member via an undocumented param, widening attack surface for the pagination flaw to audit-log data.

findings.title: BasePaginator now passes negative offset for prev cursors to queryset slice
findings.body: BasePaginator.get_result was changed from queryset[offset:stop] to max(0,offset) only when not is_prev, leaving queryset[offset:stop] with a potentially negative offset when is_prev is true. Any crafted cursor with negative offset and is_prev can trigger Django's negative-slicing assertion or inconsistent prev-page trimming, causing errors or wrong pages.

findings.title: Silent hardcoded eviction truncates segments during insert
findings.body: The script now does if span_count > 1000 then zpopmin(set_key, span_count-1000) with a hardcoded 1000. This silently drops the oldest spans by end_timestamp_precise on every insert, with no metric or log, and disagrees with SpansBuffer max_segment_spans default 1001. It replaces the previous explicit skip-and-log path and causes undetectable data loss under large traces.

findings.title: Removal of max_segment_spans enforcement and observability
findings.body: _load_segment_data no longer checks len(payloads[key]) > max_segment_spans, increments spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded, or logs. Oversized segments are now silently truncated at insert time in Lua, so the configurable limit is dead code and operators lose visibility into dropped-span conditions.

findings.title: Unvalidated end_timestamp_precise causes consumer crash
findings.body: process_batch does val["end_timestamp_precise"] with a direct dict subscript to populate the new required Span.end_timestamp_precise used as Redis ZADD score. Any span event missing or with null/non-numeric precise timestamp raises KeyError/TypeError and crashes the batch, whereas the old path only needed payload bytes. There is no fallback to now or validation before ZADD.

findings.title: Redirect traversal limit cut from 10000 to 1000 fragments deep traces
findings.body: The redirect-chase loop was reduced from for i=0,10000 to for i=0,1000 without justification. Traces/segments with redirect chains deeper than 1000 will stop early with wrong set_span_id, leaving span buffers unmerged and producing duplicated or split segments on flush.
